text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high OOM rate observed in serving-hotpool-7 during prefill path. 42 container restarts in last 5m. Paging oncall @sam :rotating_light:

sam: on it, joining. Which customers impacted?

maria-cs: seeing a spike in errors for a customer running very large context prompts (40k+ tokens). They reported streaming disconnects.

devon: logs attached, looks like CUDA OOM on prefill stage, repeated in the first 30s of start. snippet:
```
2026-03-17T21:15:02Z ERROR runtime: PrefillOOM: allocation failed 26.3GB > free 24.8GB
stack: 0x7f3a1c... cudaMalloc failed at prefill_kv_alloc
container restart triggered by healthcheck: exit code 137
```

carla: thanks. quick mitigation options: 1) disable long-prefill flag for requests > 32k tokens; 2) route large-context requests to fallback-cpu or smaller model; 3) temporarly reduce max_prefill_workers on hotpool-7.

anika: also can toggle kv_cache_eviction to aggressive (ttl=30s) to reduce resident KV memory during prefill. Might degrade repeat-turn perf but prevents OOM.

sam: executing mitigations now. disabling prefill for >32k via featureflag-rollout:
```bash
/rollout feature disable prefill-large-context --env production --threshold 32k
```

sam: routing traffic for known heavy-customer to fallback-model v1.9-quant (lower mem).

carla: running a drain on the most-affected nodes to recycle containers more gracefully:
```bash
kubectl cordon node/gpu-72 && kubectl drain node/gpu-72 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

devon: note: hotpool-7 has some noisy neighbors — several long-prefill jobs queued concurrently. Suggest backpressure at the gateway for requests with context > 16k while we stabilize.

anika: enabling kv eviction and reducing per-request kv window to 32k for the pool now (hotpatch rolling):
```yaml
hotpool-7:
  kv_window: 32768
  kv_eviction: aggressive
```

sam: changes applied. observed error rate falling from 6.2% -> 0.9% over last 2m. containers still restarting occasionally but much less frequent. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident acknowledged by sam. escalation level: P2.

maria-cs: drafting customer-facing note: "We observed container restarts impacting very long-context prompts. We applied temporary routing and cache eviction mitigations to stabilize; investigating root cause and will follow up with timeline."

carla: handoff to night oncall @carla for monitoring and follow-up root-cause. Next steps: collect full coredumps from restarted containers, histogram of token-lengths causing prefill allocations, and check whether kernel-level fragmentation contributed.

sam: attaching quick triage checklist for followup:
- collect kernel dmesg and nvml logs from nodes that restarted
- export sample requests (anonymized) that triggered OOMs
- run a reproduce job with stress tool on a staging replica

devon: queued a job to reproduce with mixed concurrent large-prefill runs. will add results to the incident doc.

carla: leaving monitoring alerts on; if restarts > 5/min or error rate > 2% in next 30m, escalate to infra oncall.

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: mitigations applied, customer routing done, degradation reduced. Monitoring continues.

sam: locking thread for handoff notes, moving to postmortem drafting. thanks all. :handshake:
